question: A consultant has an hour to review a long research brief before sending it to a client. Which sequence should she follow?
options: A) Read the conclusion; identify the claims the conclusion rests on; check those claims; verify the supporting detail.
B) Check those claims; verify the supporting detail; identify the claims the conclusion rests on; read the conclusion.
C) Identify the claims the conclusion rests on; verify the supporting detail; read the conclusion; check those claims.
D) Verify the supporting detail; read the conclusion; identify the claims the conclusion rests on; check those claims.
correct_answers: A) Read the conclusion; identify the claims the conclusion rests on; check those claims; verify the supporting detail.
explanations: Correct. Reading the conclusion first reveals what the brief is asking the client to accept, which identifies the load-bearing claims. Those are checked while time remains, and remaining detail is verified with whatever is left.
Checking claims that have not yet been identified is not possible, and reading the conclusion last leaves the review with no organising purpose.
The claims a conclusion rests on cannot be identified before the conclusion has been read, so this ordering starts from an unknown.
Starting on supporting detail spends the scarce hour on material that may not matter, and the conclusion is read only after that time is gone.
